title: Lock instead of suspending on the IdeaPad Slim 3 15AMN8
head: 14dd5215dc2f
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: An existing external-power lid policy can bypass the new lock on an undocked 82XQ
leads.consequence: Conditional on another drop-in explicitly setting HandleLidSwitchExternalPower=suspend or suspend-then-hibernate, closing the affected laptop's lid while plugged in still invokes that sleep action. Both emitted drop-ins set only HandleLidSwitch=lock. The systemd default is no explicit external-power action, so the stock configuration without another drop-in is not affected. Account for this other key before claiming lid close cannot suspend on AC; do not change the docked/clamshell ignore default.
leads.triage: dropped; No config at head sets ExternalPower (git grep); reachable only via user config or unmerged PRs, covered by B2/B3; factual

leads.summary: Open hibernation-policy PR #12125 installs a later logind drop-in that defeats this model-specific drop-in
leads.consequence: If both PRs merge and hibernation is configured on a Lenovo 82XQ, PR #12125's setup or migration installs /etc/systemd/logind.conf.d/99-omarchy-lid-sleep.conf after the IdeaPad's 50-ideapad-suspend.conf. logind uses the later HandleLidSwitch=suspend-then-hibernate on battery and HandleLidSwitchExternalPower=suspend on AC. The regression exists irrespective of which PR merges first once both drop-ins are installed; this PR's matching hardware check and success marker do not prevent the later policy. Coordinate an exclusion or higher-priority model-specific override, including AC behavior.
leads.triage: published; Coordinator verified the PR is open and its diff; Opus confirmed effective behaviour and that AllowSuspend=no covers it (opus/followup-related-prs.md). Published conditionally under F2; factual+behavioural

leads.summary: Open lid-debounce PR #12210 adds a separate systemctl suspend path that this drop-in cannot intercept
leads.consequence: With both PRs merged, on an undocked 82XQ with suspend-off disabled (default), Hyprland's lid-close handler from #12210 starts a timer that calls systemctl suspend after three seconds if the lid remains closed. A logind HandleLidSwitch=lock does not stop that explicit request; on AC, #12210's HandleLidSwitchExternalPower=ignore also prevents this PR's inherited lock. The delay policy's own 30-lid-ignore.conf is overridden by the IdeaPad 50- key on battery, so the two PRs' tests can both pass while the effective merged lid behavior is wrong. Make the new lid-suspend helper respect this model's no-suspend condition, and reconcile the AC action.
leads.triage: published; Coordinator verified the diff; Opus confirmed. Published conditionally under F2; factual+behavioural

leads.summary: Missing DMI identity fields cause a success-shaped, unreported skip
leads.consequence: Conditional on an otherwise affected device having unreadable or absent sys_vendor or product_name at install/migration time, the installer records this hardware step as successful, and the per-user migration runner can create a completed marker even though the protective drop-in was not written. No diagnostic tells the user that the suspend workaround did not apply. Matching hardware with complete readable DMI fields is unaffected. A warning/retry signal for incomplete identity, especially when the other field identifies the relevant model/vendor, would distinguish this from genuinely different hardware.
leads.triage: dropped; Requires absent DMI on real affected hardware, which is not established; low value; behavioural

flags.why: Drop-ins are parsed in filename order and each Allow* key is a plain tristate assignment, so a later-sorting drop-in still wins; explicit no only overrides sleep.conf and earlier-sorting drop-ins.
flags.fix: Setting AllowSuspendThenHibernate=no and AllowHybridSleep=no explicitly also overrides sleep.conf or an earlier-sorting drop-in that turns them on.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up at `14dd5215` to the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13115#issuecomment-5824747928) and the [author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13115#issuecomment-5825344286). Two of the four earlier findings are resolved and two are unchanged. No regressions from the new commit were found.

| Earlier finding | Status at `14dd5215` |
|---|---|
| `HandleLidSwitchDocked=lock` inverts the clamshell design | Resolved |
| Test calls the host's `systemctl`; two assertions cannot fail | Resolved (small remaining test gap, below) |
| Migration is marked complete when `sudo` fails | Still present |
| Other suspend paths remain reachable on the 82XQ | Still present |

**Verified:**
- `HandleLidSwitchDocked=lock` is gone from both scripts, so a docked lid close keeps logind's default `ignore`. The test asserts the key is absent from the installer's drop-in.
- In an isolated run with a canary `sudo`/`systemctl` placed first on the `PATH` the test inherits, the new test never reached the canary and passed 6/6. The previous test called it once (`systemctl reload systemd-logind`).
- Each of these mutations now fails the test, as intended:
  - removing the migration's `-f` guard or its DMI guards
  - removing the reload, or changing it to `restart`
  - removing `[Login]` or `HandleSuspendKeyLongPress=lock` from the installer's drop-in
- Apart from the two removed lines and the test rewrite, the installer and migration are byte-identical to the previously reviewed head.

The reply's statement that `[Login]` and `HandleSuspendKeyLongPress` are now asserted holds for the installer's drop-in only (see the test note below).

### Migration is still marked complete when `sudo` fails

`migrations/1790227635.sh` line 16 is unchanged: `sudo install -d -m 0755 "$conf_dir" || exit 0`. The runner (`bin/omarchy-migrate` lines 91-95) writes the completion marker whenever a migration exits 0. The reload on line 28 still ends in `>/dev/null 2>&1 || true`.

Isolated runs through the real `bin/omarchy-migrate` at this head, with stubbed `sudo`/`systemctl` and synthetic LENOVO/82XQ DMI:

| Case | migrate exit | Marker | Drop-in | `--pending` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| every `sudo` call fails | 0 | written | absent | nothing listed |
| only `sudo tee` fails | 1 | none | absent | lists the migration |
| reload fails | 0 | written | present | nothing listed, no message |
| `\|\| exit 0` removed, `sudo` fails | 1 | none | absent | lists the migration |

**Impact:** on an affected 82XQ, one failed password prompt (for example from the login notifier or a manual `omarchy-migrate`) permanently skips the fix for that user. This conflicts with `agents/skills/migrations.md` line 129 ("A migration that cannot finish must exit non-zero, remain pending, and stop the queue"). During `omarchy update`, sudo is usually already authenticated by the package step, so that path is less likely to hit it.

**Suggested change:** drop `|| exit 0` from line 16. The current test still passes 6/6 with that change. For the reload, the pattern in `migrations/1784970000.sh` lines 18-25 applies: logind exposes `HandleLidSwitch` as a property, so the migration can compare it and set `reboot-required` on a mismatch.

### Other suspend paths still reach suspend on the 82XQ

Nothing in this area changed. The drop-in covers only logind's lid and suspend-key handling. The System menu's Suspend entry (`default/omarchy/omarchy-menu.jsonc` line 38) still runs `systemctl suspend`, and `systemctl suspend` still suspends. In systemd v262, the hibernate key falls back to regular suspend when hibernation is not set up, and hibernation is opt-in in Omarchy. The code comments still say suspend "can never succeed on this model". Whether the 82XQ keyboard has a sleep or hibernate key was not verified.

Two open PRs would also bypass this drop-in on the 82XQ if they merge (from the PR diffs and systemd v262 source; not run):

| Open PR | Effect on an undocked 82XQ with this PR |
|---|---|
| #12210 (lid-close debounce) | Its lid helper runs `systemctl suspend` after about 3 s unless `suspend-off` is enabled, on battery and on AC |
| #12125 (lid sleep policy), hibernation set up | Its `99-omarchy-lid-sleep.conf` sorts after `50-ideapad-suspend.conf`: suspend-then-hibernate on battery, suspend on AC |

**Impact:** a user on an affected 82XQ who picks Suspend from the System menu still hits the NVMe failure the PR is meant to prevent. The same applies to lid close if either PR above merges, under the conditions in the table.

**Suggested change:** if the goal is that this model never suspends, a model-gated `/etc/systemd/sleep.conf.d/` drop-in with `[Sleep]` `AllowSuspend=no` covers every path above, whatever the logind drop-in order:
- By default it also disallows suspend-then-hibernate and hybrid sleep. Hibernate stays available.
- logind ignores a disallowed lid or key action.
- `systemctl suspend` fails with "Sleep verb 'suspend' is disabled by config".
- The sleep config is re-read on every request, so this needs no logind reload.
- Setting `AllowSuspendThenHibernate=no` and `AllowHybridSleep=no` explicitly also overrides `sleep.conf` or an earlier-sorting drop-in that turns them on.

To also hide the menu entry, the migration (which runs per user) could set Omarchy's existing `suspend-off` toggle. If the narrower lid-and-key scope is intentional, rewording the comments would avoid overstating the protection.

**Optional test improvement:** the test checks the migration's drop-in only for `HandleLidSwitch=lock` (line 78). In mutation runs, removing `[Login]`, `HandleSuspendKey=lock` or `HandleSuspendKeyLongPress=lock` from the migration's heredoc, or adding `HandleLidSwitchDocked=lock` there, still passed 6/6. The two heredocs are byte-identical today, but nothing enforces that. A `cmp "$dropin" "$migration_dropin"` would cover it. A failing-`sudo` case that expects a non-zero migration exit would lock in the fix above.

**Open question, drive or model:** issue #12887 documents one unit, with Micron `MTFDKCD512QGN-1BN1AABLA` firmware `1001V8LN`, and attributes the fault to that drive's firmware. Lenovo's PSREF for the IdeaPad Slim 3 15AMN8 lists 128 GB to 1 TB SSD options in one M.2 slot, so this model ships with more than one drive. The PR gates on `LENOVO`/`82XQ` only. If the fault is drive-specific, unaffected 82XQ units lose lid-close suspend for no benefit. One report cannot settle whether it is. Reports from 82XQ units with other drives would. Options: also match `/sys/class/nvme/nvme*/model` (and optionally `firmware_rev`), or state the model-wide assumption in the comments.
